examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{塾|じゅく}に{通|かよ}わせている。
examples.english: I am sending my child to cram school.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}が{終|お}わってから、{塾|じゅく}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I go to cram school after school ends.

examples.japanese: {受験|じゅけん}{対策|たいさく}のために{塾|じゅく}で{勉強|べんきょう}している。
examples.english: I am studying at cram school for entrance exam preparation.

notes:
{塾|じゅく} is a private after-school tutoring institution, extremely common in Japan for exam preparation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {塾|じゅく}に{通|かよ}う (attend cram school)
- {塾|じゅく}に{行|い}く (go to cram school)
- {塾|じゅく}の{先生|せんせい} (cram school teacher)
- {塾|じゅく}の{宿題|しゅくだい} (cram school homework)

TYPES OF {塾|じゅく}:
- {学習|がくしゅう}{塾|じゅく} (tutoring for general subjects)
- {進学|しんがく}{塾|じゅく} (exam prep school)
- {英会話|えいかいわ}{塾|じゅく} (English conversation school)
- {個別|こべつ}{指導|しどう}{塾|じゅく} (individual tutoring school)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Most Japanese students attend {塾|じゅく} after regular school hours, especially before entrance exams. This is a major part of Japan's education-focused culture.
